create.name: Anushka Fernandopulle
create.bio:
Anushka Fernandopulle is a teacher of insight meditation in the Theravada Buddhist tradition, based in the San Francisco Bay Area. She studied Buddhism at Harvard and then spent four years in full-time meditation practice in the United States, India and Sri Lanka. She was first invited to teach in 1998, went on to complete a four-year teacher training whose leaders included Jack Kornfield and Joseph Goldstein, and has sat on the teachers' council at Spirit Rock since 2011.

She leads residential retreats of a weekend to a month, including retreats on loving-kindness and insight and retreats for LGBTQIA+ practitioners, at centres in California, Massachusetts and British Columbia. Alongside retreat teaching she gives everyday talks that apply the Buddha's teaching to modern life, from shopping and technology to sport and the news, many of them freely available online. She also works as an organisational consultant and leadership coach, with an MBA from Yale, bringing mindfulness into workplaces and leadership programmes, and she has written for Tricycle, Lion's Roar and Inquiring Mind.

courses.title: February Monthlong Insight Meditation Retreat, Spirit Rock
courses.description: A month of silent residential insight meditation practice in California, listed on her teaching schedule for February 2027. It is an application retreat, and she suggests some prior class and daylong experience before a long retreat.

free_resources.title: Talks
free_resources.description: Her page of free recorded dharma talks, gathered by theme: everyday life, the eightfold path, the heart practices and more, with links on to her retreat talks.

free_resources.title: Anushka Fernandopulle's talks on Dharma Seed
free_resources.description: The archive of her retreat talks and guided meditations, free to stream or download.

free_resources.title: What Is Mindfulness?
free_resources.description: A short introduction on her site to mindfulness as a trainable quality of mind rooted in the Pali word sati, with reading suggestions and a short video.
